meta.changelog_v3: Replaced the v2 market_rate_position/adjustments delta system with a direct, simpler formula: market_benchmark = market midpoint; recommended_freight = market_weight*market_benchmark + cost_weight*cost_floor, floored at cost_floor (never below). Market comparison now uses recommended_freight, not customer_pays (commission no longer distorts the market-competitiveness read). Removed the maximum_driver_margin_pct hard clamp on driver payout — driver_payout now equals recommended_freight directly, margin is reported (never forced down), with target/maximum margin kept only as reference figures. Added MARKET_BELOW_COST_FLOOR / market_vs_cost_status. Split maintenance and depreciation into separate cost lines (previously combined); split insurance and permits into separate overhead lines. Revised heavy-vehicle loaded mileage upward (v2's 3.5 km/l for a 16-20T truck was on the pessimistic end of the single source found; 4.0-5.0 km/l is used per operator-reported ranges, flagged as an adjusted assumption pending real fleet data). Renamed several config keys to match this spec exactly (grain_rate_per_tonne, overnight_allowance, average_driving_hours_per_day, maximum_fraction_of_freight, empty_return.{no_backhaul,established_corridor,thin_corridor,default}).

update_frequency_guidance.tolls: Update monthly, or replace with live toll-routing API output per trip.
update_frequency_guidance.vehicle_classes.*.market_rate_per_km_ran: Update monthly — these move faster than cost inputs.
update_frequency_guidance.driver / overheads / vehicle_classes mai: Update quarterly, ideally against real fleet telemetry.
update_frequency_guidance.pricing_model / platform: Business decision — revisit quarterly against acceptance-rate and market data.

value_type_legend.observed: Directly reported by a named source on/near the stated date.
value_type_legend.researched_estimate: Derived from a range/benchmark reported by sources; a point estimate was chosen and is labeled as such.
value_type_legend.assumption: Not directly sourced; a modelling assumption made for lack of exact data, flagged for review.
value_type_legend.business_decision: A target/policy value supplied for this system rather than an external market observation.

diesel_price_per_litre.source: The Hans India, fuel price roundup
diesel_price_per_litre.note: National average the same day was ~₹97.8/L (Goodreturns). Swap in the local city rate when known. Overridable per-call via diesel_price_override.

mini_lcv.label: Mini/LCV truck (Tata Ace/407, Ashok Leyland Dost class)

max_payload_kg.source: OEM payload spec range for Tata 407-class LCVs, TruckJunction, 2026.

mileage_loaded_kmpl.source: Tata 407 Gold SFC unladen-tested mileage 6.9-10 kmpl (TruckJunction); reduced ~15-20% for typical load.

mileage_empty_kmpl.source: Same basis, empty closer to tested kmpl.

maintenance_per_km.source: TruckGuru: ₹2-3/km maintenance & tyres for medium trucks, scaled down for a smaller LCV.

depreciation_per_km.source: EMI/depreciation ₹20,000-50,000/month (TruckGuru) ÷ ~4,000-6,000 km/month for a small operator.

max_payload_kg.source: Freight-rate tables (Shipzip/Okararoadways), 'Medium Trucks (9-12 ton)' band, upper bound used, 2026.

mileage_loaded_kmpl.source: Ashok Leyland Partner 6-Tyre unladen mileage 8.5 kmpl (TruckJunction), reduced ~18% for typical load.

mileage_empty_kmpl.source: TruckJunction, Ashok Leyland Partner 6-Tyre mileage spec.

max_payload_kg.source: Shipzip '10-Wheeler Trucks (16-20 ton)' band, upper bound used, 2025-26.

mileage_loaded_kmpl.source: ADJUSTED (v3): BiggWheels TCO guide cited ~3.5 km/l for 12-tyre configs (2026), but that was the only single source found and sits at the pessimistic end of operator-reported ranges. 4.5 km/l is used per a 4.0-5.0 km/l operator-reported range for well-maintained BS6 heavy trucks on good highway stretches; still flagged for validation against real fleet telemetry.

mileage_empty_kmpl.source: Interpolated ~20-25% better than loaded, standard heavy-truck behaviour, scaled from the adjusted loaded figure above.

maintenance_per_km.source: Scaled up from TruckGuru ₹2-3/km benchmark for higher axle/tyre count.

depreciation_per_km.source: Scaled from Fleetable's ₹8-15/km all-in TCO benchmark, net of fuel/toll/driver/maintenance shares.

max_payload_kg.source: Shipzip 'Multi-Axle & Container Trucks (20-40 ton)' band, mid-upper bound used, 2025-26.

mileage_loaded_kmpl.source: ADJUSTED (v3): BiggWheels cited ~2.5 km/l for 18-tyre setups (2026); raised toward the middle of a plausible 3.0-4.0 km/l operator-reported range for well-maintained rigs, consistent with the same upward revision applied to heavy_10w. Flagged for validation against real fleet telemetry.

maintenance_per_km.source: Scaled from TruckGuru benchmark for the largest vehicle class.

depreciation_per_km.source: FR8.in: financed 32ft MXL container fixed costs spread over 6,000-8,000 km/month typical utilisation.

reefer_medium.label: Refrigerated medium truck (7-9T box, fruit & vegetable long-haul)

max_payload_kg.note: Slightly below base_class max_payload_kg — insulation panels and the reefer unit add tare weight, reducing usable payload versus an equivalent non-reefer body.

reefer_heavy.label: Refrigerated heavy truck (12-19T box, long-haul fruit/vegetable/dairy)

max_payload_kg.note: Slightly below base_class max_payload_kg for the same insulation/reefer-unit tare-weight reason.

preferred_utilization_pct.note: Target load factor — close to full without zero slack.

maximum_utilization_pct.note: Hard ceiling. required_capacity_kg = shipment_weight_kg / 0.90; a vehicle only qualifies if its max_payload_kg >= required_capacity_kg. Equivalently: a vehicle's SAFE capacity is max_payload_kg x 0.90 — a shipment must not exceed that.

minimum_headroom_kg.note: Extra absolute-kg safety margin required on top of the utilization ceiling, mainly relevant for the smallest vehicle class.

market_weight.note: Weight given to the market benchmark (the published mid rate x distance) when forming recommended_freight.

cost_weight.note: Weight given to cost_floor when forming recommended_freight. market_weight + cost_weight should sum to 1.0.

market_rate_position.note: Retained for future use/documentation only. The current formula uses the configured mid value from market_rate_per_km_range directly as market_benchmark, NOT a recomputed low+position*(high-low) interpolation, so this field does not currently change engine output.

minimum_driver_margin_pct.note: Enforced: recommended_freight can never fall below operating_cost x (1 + this).

target_driver_margin_pct.note: Reference/analysis figure only — reported alongside the actual margin achieved, not used to force a specific driver_payout.

maximum_driver_margin_pct.note: Reference/analysis figure only (v3 no longer clamps driver_payout to this — a favourable market can legitimately pay the driver more; the figure is reported for monitoring, not enforced as a ceiling).

fallback_truck_per_plaza.source: assureshift.in: NHAI toll rates for heavy vehicles typically ₹250-400/plaza, 2026.

fallback_lcv_per_plaza.note: No single published all-India LCV/Class-2 average found; modelled at ~55-60% of the truck-class fee per NHAI's axle-based tiering.

average_plaza_spacing_km.note: Derived from cited corridor tolls (~₹3-5/km cumulative, Okararoadways) divided by the per-plaza fee; used only as a fallback when plaza count is unknown.

return_toll_recovery_pct.source: TollGuru/NHAI note a discounted return-trip rate applies within ~24h at many plazas; exact discount varies by plaza, so this is a conservative modelling assumption for the discount itself (separate from empty_return, which governs how much of that discounted return toll the customer bears).

local_day_rate.source: Indeed India: avg. truck driver salary ₹20,460/month (25th-75th pctile ₹10,434-₹40,121), 2026, converted to a ~26-working-day basis.

long_haul_day_rate.source: assureshift.in: driver wages add ₹2,400-3,600 to a 3-day Delhi-Mumbai trip (≈₹800-1,200/day bata), 2026.

overnight_allowance.note: Separate night-out allowance paid on top of running bata; not independently sourced at a specific figure.

second_driver_distance_threshold_km.note: One-way distance beyond which a relief/second driver is added; all-India regulatory driving-hour limits are not centrally published in a single source, so this is a conservative planning assumption.

average_speed_kmph.note: Blended average accounting for highway + city driving + loading/mandi delays. Not independently sourced as a single figure. Combined with average_driving_hours_per_day this gives achievable same-day distance and multi-day trip length; used instead of a hardcoded km threshold.

annual_insurance.source: TruckGuru: commercial vehicle insurance ₹30,000-80,000/year depending on truck type and insured value, 2026.

annual_permits.source: TruckGuru: interstate permits, fitness certificates, national permits ₹15,000-50,000/year, 2026.

trips_per_year.note: Assumed revenue-trip count used only to amortise the two annual fixed costs above into a per-trip figure; tune once real fleet-utilisation data exists.

grain_rate_per_tonne.source: AP Civil Supplies hamali wage ₹28/quintal (=₹280/tonne) for loading/unloading foodgrain, The Hans India, Sep-2026 (union sought revision to ₹40/quintal = ₹400/tonne).

perishable_multiplier.note: Vegetables: careful crate handling vs. sacked grain. No published India-wide differential rate exists; flagged for calibration against real operator data.

fruit_multiplier.note: Fruits: stricter handling than vegetables (bruising risk), slightly higher than the vegetable multiplier.

grain_multiplier.note: The base hamali rate above was itself observed for sacked/bulk foodgrain, so no uplift is applied.

maximum_fraction_of_freight.note: Handling cost is capped at this fraction of market_freight_mid so a large per-tonne handling charge on a small load cannot distort the quote.

reefer_rules.note: No single published India-wide threshold exists for when refrigeration becomes necessary; these are modelling assumptions based on general cold-chain literature, flagged for per-commodity refinement.

fruits.note: Stricter (lower) thresholds than vegetables — most fruit is more perishable/bruise-prone than hardier vegetables (potato, onion), though this varies a lot by specific item.

rice.note: Never auto-selected; only used if force_reefer=True explicitly overrides.

fuel_penalty_pct.source: Okararoadways: 'refrigerated trucks cost 10-15% more' than standard trucking on the same route, 2026 — applied once per leg, to the fuel line only, representing genset/cooling energy draw.

additional_maintenance_per_km.note: Extra upkeep for the refrigeration unit itself, distinct from the fuel-energy cost above.

additional_depreciation_per_km.source: Rinac 2026: a 20-40ft reefer container/body adds ₹5-15 lakh over a standard body — this is the amortised per-km cost of that extra capex, distinct from both the fuel penalty and the elevated reefer market rate (which reflects market perception/scarcity, not the operator's own cost).

empty_return.logic: backhaul_available=True -> recovery = no_backhaul (0%, the return leg is covered by a paying backhaul so the customer bears none of it). backhaul_available=False -> recovery = established_corridor (15%) or thin_corridor (30%) depending on corridor_type, or `default` (30%) if corridor_type is unrecognised. Forward and return legs are each computed once, over the one-way distance, using leg-specific parameters (empty mileage, discounted toll, symmetric driver-days) — never by doubling total distance and then also applying a recovery percentage on top.

no_backhaul.note: Applied when backhaul_available=True — despite the key name, this represents 'no [customer-borne] empty-return cost', not 'backhaul unavailable'.

established_corridor.note: Well-travelled corridors (state/district-capital pairs, mandi-to-city routes) where backhaul is likely even if not pre-booked.

thin_corridor.note: One-way-heavy or remote routes. Lowered from the earlier 50% assumption per explicit instruction not to use that figure as a default.

default.note: Used when corridor_type is neither 'established' nor 'thin'.

maximum_recovery_pct.note: Hard safety clamp — recovery_pct is never allowed to exceed this, regardless of corridor_type input.

gta_rate_without_itc_pct.source: TruckGuru: GST on GTA services is 5% without ITC or 12% with ITC; most SME shippers use the 5% no-ITC option, 2026.
gta_rate_without_itc_pct.note: Typically payable by the registered consignor/consignee under reverse charge — shown separately, not folded into 'customer_pays'.

commission_pct.source: BlackBuck charges 10-20% commission on freight value; Porter charges 15-20% (multiple sources, 2026). Set to 0 per explicit instruction: the platform is paying the driver for a transport service, not selling freight as its own product, so freight is passed through to the buyer at cost with no markup. The platform's cut is taken from the farmer's crop-value share instead (see consumer_pricing_engine.py) — kept configurable here in case a logistics-side commission is reintroduced later.

minimum_fare.note: Floor so genuinely small trips still cover driver call-out and basic overheads; applied only when the computed customer_pays falls below it.

below_market_max_ratio.note: recommended_freight_per_km / market_mid_per_km below this ratio -> BELOW_MARKET.

above_market_max_ratio.note: Between competitive_max_ratio and this -> ABOVE_MARKET; beyond this -> SIGNIFICANTLY_ABOVE_MARKET.
